item.title: Dutch privacy watchdog fines Uber €825m over drivers’ rights
item.description:
Dutch privacy watchdog fines Uber €825m over drivers’ rights

August 21, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Dutch data protection authority AP has fined Uber €825 million for deactivating drivers’ accounts through automated systems without properly informing them, in what is the second-largest penalty ever issued under European privacy law.

The watchdog leads on privacy oversight of Uber across the EU because the company’s European head office is in Amsterdam.

Under the EU’s data protection rules, companies are not allowed to let an algorithm alone take decisions that significantly affect someone’s life. A human must be involved, and the person affected must be able to object.

The case relates to events between 2020 and 2022 and began with complaints from drivers in France, who had been suspended on suspicion of fraud, such as taking unnecessary detours to increase their fares.

Uber to appeal
Uber said it would challenge the fine. “We strongly disagree with this decision and disproportionate fine,” a spokesperson told Reuters, adding that the company took drivers’ rights seriously.

The firm said its current policies included human review and allowed drivers to contest suspensions, and that it no longer deactivated accounts permanently through automated systems alone.

The penalty easily exceeds the AP’s previous record, a €290 million fine imposed on Uber last year for transferring drivers’ data to the United States.

That case, which Uber is also appealing, grew out of the same complaints by French drivers. The regulator had already fined the company €10 million in early 2024 over drivers’ privacy rights and €600,000 in 2018.

The only larger fine under the EU’s General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) is the €1.2 billion penalty handed to Meta by Ireland’s regulator in 2023, for transferring European Facebook users’ data to the United States, a case that Meta is appealing.

item.title: Wall Street Journal tips Groningen novelist for Nobel prize
item.description:
Wall Street Journal tips Groningen novelist for Nobel prize

August 21, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Wall Street Journal has named the Groningen-based novelist Anjet Daanje a serious contender for the Nobel prize in literature, in a review of her novel Het lied van ooievaar en dromedaris (The Song of Stork and Dromedary), first published in 2022 and recently translated to English.

The paper’s critic Sam Sacks said Daanje is “one of the continent’s leading writers.”

Sacks noted that the prize has never gone to a writer from the Netherlands, which he put down to bad luck rather than any lack of quality. He named the late Harry Mulisch as another Dutch author who deserved it.

The last Dutch author nominated was Simon Vestdijk, who received multiple nominations in the 1950s and 60s. The Nobel archive is sealed for 50 years, so any more recent candidates remain secret.

Inspired by the Brontës
Daanje, who was born in Drenthe, achieved a breakthrough with her novel Deherdenking soldaat (The Remembered Soldier) in 2019.

Het lied van ooievaar en dromedaris won both the Libris literature prize and the Boekenbon prize – the first book to take the Netherlands’ two main literary awards. Daanje went on to receive the Constantijn Huygens prize for her body of work.

The English edition runs to more than 700 pages. Loosely based on the Brontë sisters, it circles an Emily Brontë-like writer through interlinked stories spanning almost three centuries.

The 2026 Nobel prize in literature will be announced in Stockholm on October 8.

item.title: Cabinet still aims for majority budget support, Heinen says
item.description:
Cabinet still aims for majority budget support, Heinen says

August 21, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Dutch cabinet still believes it can win support from across the political spectrum for its annual budget, finance minister Eelco Heinen has said, a week before the plans are due to be sent off for review.

“I’m confident that will work out,” Heinen told reporters ahead of Friday’s cabinet meeting. “We’re now really in the final phase.” He said he believed the opposition parties whose votes are needed are moving closer together and “don’t differ that much from each other.”

Heinen, who stayed away from the opening days of talks with opposition leaders this week, is now holding his own discussions with the parties. The cabinet wants a deal in place by next Friday, August 28, when it plans to send the budget to the Council of State.

Left or right
The minority coalition of D66, VVD and CDA is 10 seats short of a majority in the lower house and holds less than a third of the seats in the senate, leaving it reliant on opposition votes.

Support from opposition party PRO, which has 20 seats, would give it a comfortable majority, while a deal with the far-right JA21, which has nine seats, would leave it one short and dependent on a third party.

PRO, JA21 and the orthodox Protestant SGP have all said the cabinet will eventually have to choose between a majority on the left or on the right. But Heinen has resisted that, backing a call this week by Christian-social ChristenUnie leader Mirjam Bikker for the parties to drop the left-right divide and judge the plans on their merits.

Welfare cuts
Talks with PRO, the most straightforward route to a majority, remain difficult. After a meeting on Thursday, the party’s finance spokesperson Luc Stultiens said he had seen little movement “and that will be needed if you want our support.”

PRO wants the cabinet to scrap €6.5 billion in planned cuts to social security and raise the money through higher taxes on wealth and corporations instead. Its position is backed by the unions, which have called a national public transport strike on September 9 in protest at the reforms.

JA21 and the SGP, which are working together, met ministers again on Friday morning, with the ChristenUnie due later in the day. The budget is set to be presented on Prinsjesdag, September 15.

item.title: Government condemns Israeli West Bank settlement plan
item.description:
Government condemns Israeli West Bank settlement plan

August 21, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Netherlands has joined six other governments in condemning Israel’s decision to open bidding on a major settlement project in the occupied West Bank, and called on the Netanyahu regime to withdraw the plans immediately.

Prime minister Rob Jetten and the leaders of Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy and Norway called the project “unacceptable” in a joint statement, and said they have “grave concerns” over the potential impact it could have on achieving peace in the region, particularly amid “unprecedented levels of violence by settlers against civilians.”

Israel’s construction and housing ministry opened bidding on Tuesday for 1,234 homes, part of a wider plan for 3,401 settler homes in E1, an area east of Jerusalem. Contractors have until October 19 to bid, a week before Israeli elections.

Critics say the project would split the West Bank in two and cut East Jerusalem off from it, making a contiguous Palestinian state impossible.

The condemnation comes as the Netherlands prepares to enforce its own ban on settlement goods, which takes effect on September 22. The three-year measure bars the import, sale and trade of goods from illegal settlements in the occupied territories.

The Netherlands is also the main EU entry point for produce grown in Israeli settlements, according to research published in June, handling around a third of such shipments reaching the bloc.

Settlements in the occupied West Bank are illegal under international law. The E1 plan, approved last year, faces a legal challenge in Israel, where a court has asked the state to respond to the petitions by September 1.

item.title: Police shooting in Sittard wounds Nijmegen man
item.description:
Police shooting in Sittard wounds Nijmegen man

August 21, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Police in Sittard in Limburg shot a man outside the city’s police station on Stationsplein overnight Friday due to what they called a “suspicious situation”.

The suspect, a 34-year-old man from Nijmegen, was injured in the leg and received first aid on the scene. He was then arrested and transferred to hospital.

Police shootings are rare in the Netherlands. Last year, officers shot at people 15 times.

Still, the national police are investigating the incident, as all cases involving an officer shooting that results in injury or death must be looked into.

Police are also looking into the cause and background of the incident.

item.title: New medicine gives hope to Dutch narcolepsy sufferers
item.description:
New medicine gives hope to Dutch narcolepsy sufferers

August 21, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Some 8,000 Dutch people suffer from narcolepsy, a sleep disorder that leaves sufferers spontaneously falling asleep during the day.

Now, for the first time, a new drug approved earlier this month in the US is being touted as the first to target the disease’s roots rather than its symptoms.

“I have been trying to give people a reasonable life for 40 years,” Gert Jan Lammers, special professor of sleep disorders at Leiden University Medical Centre, told broadcaster NOS. “With this medicine, we finally saw real improvement.”

Several of his patients participated in the drug’s research trials, and he says the results are positive. “People feel normal again. I’ve been working on this for 40 years now and I haven’t seen this before. It doesn’t work perfectly for everyone, and it doesn’t work all day, but it’s fundamentally different from what we’ve been able to do so far.”

The drug, Orzeyful (oveporexton) still has to be approved by the European Medicines Agency before being prescribed in the Netherlands, which will likely not happen until at least the end of next year.

But for those who have taken it, including Dutch trial participants who can continue using it before its approval here, it’s been a life-changer.

“It’s like you’re finally getting a good pair of glasses,” says Leontien Sickenga, who has taken the drug for one and one-half years. “With other medication I saw the world a bit better, but with this medication the world is clear. When I’m awake, I’m really there.”

In addition to falling asleep in the day, Sickenga also suffered from muscle relaxation and sleep paralysis, common in narcolepsy patients. “It’s very drastic,” she said.

How it works

According to the US Food and Drug Administration, narcolepsy “is caused by the loss of brain cells that produce orexin, a chemical messenger that regulates wakefulness, sleep, and muscle tone.”

Without orexin, the brain has trouble controlling the boundaries between sleep and waking, resulting in narcolepsy’s debilitating symptoms. But the new drug, rather than trying to relieve those symptoms, “directly activates the same brain receptor that the body’s own orexin would normally stimulate, restoring the missing signal.”

Professor of sleep diagnostics Sebastiaan Overeem, who was not involved in the drug’s research, is positive. “This is fundamentally new and very promising,” he says. “Of course, there are no miracle cures, and we still have to see how this drug works in the long run. But in the field, everyone is impressed.”

Side effects of the drug include urinating more, and it’s not yet known how effective it will be in the long-term.

“I don’t want to be too positive, because some things we can’t know yet” says Lammers. “But so far, all the signals are on green.”

item.title: Frisian asylum center to remain open, frustrating locals
item.description:
Frisian asylum center to remain open, frustrating locals

August 21, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The ministry of justice and security informed the municipality of De Fryske Marren earlier this week that the asylum seekers’ centre in Balk, which was due to permanently shut its doors on October 1 2026, will remain open for another three years, upsetting local officials.

“For the municipal executive, the following applies: a deal is a deal,” says the municipality’s website. “The fact that the agreements cannot be fulfilled now causes disappointment and frustration.”

And, reports Omrop Fryslân, will lead to legal action.

The asylum centre opened in 2016 for what was supposed to be five years. That period was extended several times, most recently in 2024, when a deal was also made to reduce the number of refugees living in the centre from 500 to 225.

While the number of asylum seekers has been reduced, refugee settlement agency COA said the lack of alternative shelters means it can’t meet the October closure deadline.

Closure not an option

“We have been looking for other solutions for as long as possible”, said COA’s Joeri Kapteijns. “However, we have the legal and social responsibility to welcome and guide people safely and with dignity. As a result, closure without an alternative is not an option.”

Closing the Balk shelter, said COA, would “mean that 300 people, families and children, will be on the streets.”

The municipality says it doesn’t want to see people on the streets, but it’s unacceptable that the deal has been broken.

“Although De Fryske Marren wants to prevent residents from being left without suitable shelter from a human point of view, it does not accept this situation,” said the municipality. “The responsibility for the residents and replacement shelter lies primarily with COA.”

But COA says the nationwide shortage of asylum spots means it takes time. “Although fewer people are registering for asylum in the Netherlands than before, the number of residents at our locations is increasing.” Some 80,000 people currently live in asylum centres.

COA attributes the problem to long asylum procedures and too few homes for people with a residence permit, meaning more people have to stay longer in shelters. “There are fewer new locations opening than there are closing,” it said.

The 300 asylum seekers in Balk, however, fulfil De Fryske Marren’s shelter obligations under the country’s distribution laws.

item.title: Ajax win at Sion, Twente lose at home in Conference League
item.description:
Ajax win at Sion, Twente lose at home in Conference League

August 21, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Ajax and FC Twente played the first legs of their Conference League play-off ties on Thursday evening, the last stage before the competition’s league phase. Ajax won 4-2 away at FC Sion in Switzerland, while Twente lost 1-0 at home to FK Qarabag.

Ajax fell behind to a goal just after 30 minutes but recovered after the break. Julian Brandt and Marcos Leonardo scored to put the visitors in front, before Sion equalised from the penalty spot through Ylyas Chouaref.

Tolu Arokodare headed in within a minute of coming on to restore the lead, and Davy Klaassen lobbed a fourth late on.

The match was shown in the Netherlands only on a €4.99 pay-per-view channel, a decision that had angered many fans in the build-up. Ajax will go through as long as they avoid losing by three or more goals in next Thursday’s return at the Johan Cruijff Arena.

Twente jeered at home
Twente had a good start in Enschede but faded, and Kady Borges scored shortly after half-time to hand Qarabag the lead. The home crowd began jeering the team, whistling at the players at full time and cheering the substitution of striker Wout Weghorst.

Qarabag, multiple-time Azerbaijani champions, reached the Champions League knockout stage last season. Both Dutch clubs had come through the previous qualifying round last week. Twente now face a difficult second leg in Baku next Thursday.

item.title: Earthquake of 2.8 shakes northern Groningen
item.description:
Earthquake of 2.8 shakes northern Groningen

August 21, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

An earthquake measuring 2.8 on the Richter scale struck the north of Groningen in the early hours of Friday, the heaviest to hit the region since March.

The epicentre was near the village of Zandeweer, in the Het Hogeland area, at a depth of three kilometres, the meteorological agency KNMI said. The quake was recorded at around 5.50am local time.

Residents in the nearby villages of Uithuizen, Kantens, Rottum and Middelstum said they had felt the tremor, broadcaster NOS reported. No damage or injuries had been reported by Friday morning.

The KNMI classed the quake as an “induced earthquake”, meaning it was caused by gas extraction. Tremors linked to drilling tend to occur closer to the surface, making them easier to feel; those measuring 1.5 and above are noticeable.

Extraction from the main Groningen field stopped two years ago, but the KNMI has warned that quakes can continue for decades as the ground settles. Gas is still being pumped from smaller fields in the province, where drilling is permitted until the end of 2032.

The last comparable tremor was a 3.0 quake near Eleveld in Drenthe in March. The strongest of the 31 induced quakes recorded near the Groningen field last year was a 3.4 tremor at Zeerijp in November, among the heaviest ever measured in the province.

item.title: Bruls calls on justice ministry to enforce motorway tractor ban
item.description:
Bruls calls on justice ministry to enforce motorway tractor ban

August 20, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Local politicians have called for nationwide rules to be enforced to keep tractors off motorways in the wake of a fatal crash during a farmers’ protest a week ago.

Hubert Bruls, mayor of Nijmegen and chair of the board of regional safety councils, said it was “incomprehensible” that local authorities took different approaches to enforcing the traffic rules.

Last Friday two people died in a collision on the A59 at the tail end of a queue that had built up on the A59 near Hees, a suburb of Nijmegen.

Police and the prosecution service had said before the collision happened that they would not prosecute farmers who drove tractors onto the motorway, even though they are prohibited, citing the right to demonstrate.

The prosecution service has since said that anyone who drives a tractor onto the motorway will be subject to enforcement, even though police said at an earlier demonstration that they did not have enough evidence to go on because the farmers had taped over their numberplates.

Bruls told NOS he wanted to hold talks with the justice ministry to decide on a national strategy for offences on the motorway.

“It’s not manageable for the police if every mayor comes up with their own guidelines and the rules change every 10 or 15 kilometres. Some things should be agreed at a regional level.

“For motorways we need to have a national approach because the motorway network covers the whole country.”

Prime minister Rob Jetten said following last week’s deadly crash it was “unacceptable” for farm vehicles to be on motorways. “It leads to very dangerous situations,” he said.
